feud_name: Killing of Þorvaldur Ósvífsson (Hallgerður's first marriage)
summary: Þorvaldur slaps Hallgerður; her foster-father Þjóstólfur avenges the blow by killing him. Ósvífur claims son-compensation and Hrútur awards 200 silver (ch.12).
After a quarrel Þjóstólfur kills Glúmur; Hrútur then kills Þjóstólfur. Glúmur's brother Þórarinn is given gifts in lieu of compensation (ch.17).
Genealogical aside: Ásgrímur became the slayer of his foster-brother Gaukur; no details given.

After the seating insult (ch.35) the two housewives have each other's servants and kinsmen killed in turn: Svartur, Kolur, Atli, Brynjólfur, Þórður leysingjason, Sigmundur. Gunnar and Njáll settle each killing; ends with Gunnar's award for Sigmundur (ch.45).

feud_name: Gunnar of Hlíðarendi vs. Otkell, Starkaður and their allies
sides: ["Hlíðarendi (Gunnar & kin)", "Gunnar's opponents (Otkell, Starkaður, Geir goði, Mörður)"]
summary: From the Kirkjubær theft and the spur-blow, through the horse-fight ambush at Knafahólar and the ambush by the two Þorgeirs, Gunnar kills repeatedly, is outlawed and killed (ch.77); Högni and Skarphéðinn avenge him (ch.79), and settlements follow (ch.80).

feud_name: Þráinn kills the outlaw viking Kolur
summary: Hákon jarl puts a price on the outlaw Kolur's head; Þráinn hunts him down in Denmark and brings his head to the earl.
Back-story: Hrappur has killed Örlygur in Iceland and flees abroad; Vopnfirðingar are entitled to prosecute.

feud_name: Hrappur affair in Norway (Hákon jarl vs. Hrappur and the Njálssons)
summary: Hrappur seduces Guðbrandur's daughter and kills his overseer, is outlawed and escapes with Þráinn; the earl turns on the Njálssons, who kill two of his men before Kári rescues them. The grievance passes to the Njálssons–Þráinn feud.
One-line aside about the man to whom Þráinn gave his ship.

The Njálssons, wronged in Norway over Hrappur and insulted at Grjótá, kill Þráinn (ch.92); his brother-in-law Lýtingur avenges him on Höskuldur Njálsson (ch.98), whose blind son Ámundi kills Lýtingur (ch.106); each is settled.

feud_name: Þangbrandur kills Þorkell in a duel
summary: Þorkell opposes the faith and challenges Þangbrandur to a duel, which Þangbrandur wins.
Veturliði speaks most against the new faith and is killed for it.
The berserk fails the fire-ordeal and is cut down by Þangbrandur and Guðleifur.

feud_name: Killing of Höskuldur Hvítanesgoði and the Burning of Njáll
sides: ["Bergþórshvoll (Njáll, sons, Kári & allies)", "Höskuldur's kin (Flosi & the burners)"]
summary: Incited by Mörður's slander, the Njálssons and Kári kill Höskuldur; Flosi, egged on by Hildigunnur, rejects the award and burns Njáll and his sons; the case ends in a battle at the Althing and a general settlement (ch.145), Kári keeps up his revenge abroad until he and Flosi are fully reconciled (ch.159).

feud_name: Kolbeinn and Egill kill Arnór Örnólfsson
summary: Back-story cited by Hildigunnur: Flosi's brothers killed Arnór at Skaftafellsþing for a minor wrong against their father.
Back-story in Skarphéðinn's taunt: after killing Ketill Skafti disguised himself and hid.
Back-story: Hallur of Síða got Flosi's kinsman Þorgrímur out of the country after he killed Halli rauði.
Óspakur steals Oddur's wethers and kills Oddur's kinsman Vali when Vali comes to seek a settlement; after a long lawsuit and the chieftains' conspiracy Óspakur is outlawed.
The outlaw Óspakur kills Már Hildisson, who had married his former wife Svala; Már's brother Bjálfi wounds Óspakur fatally on the spot. No eftirmál follows.
Long rivalry between Björn and Þórður Kolbeinsson; Björn kills Steinn in an ambush laid by Þórður, and after Björn's death the killings are settled at the Althing.

feud_name: Gísli Súrsson vs Þorgrímur and his kin
summary: Þorgrímur kills Vésteinn, Gísli Súrsson kills his brother-in-law Þorgrímur a year later, and the outlaw Gísli is finally killed by Eyjólfur the Grey (told briefly; details in Gísla saga).

feud_name: Máhlíðingamál: Þórarinn svarti vs Þorbjörn digri
sides: ["Þórarinn and Máhlíðingar", "Þorbjörn digri and Fróðá men"]
summary: A horse-theft accusation and mockery lead Þórarinn svarti to kill Þorbjörn digri and others; Snorri goði gets Þórarinn outlawed at Þórsnessþing and he goes abroad.

Arnkell and Snorri goði quarrel over the Krákunes wood; Arnkell kills Snorri's follower Haukur, and Snorri, with Þorleifur kimbi and the Þorbrandssons, kills Arnkell in revenge. The killing is settled with a three-year exile.
Gestur Þórhallsson kills Víga-Styr; Snorri's prosecution fails and leads to clashes with the Borgfirðingar. Eyrbyggja gives no motive.

A legal dispute between Hafgrímur and the brothers Brestir and Beinir ends with Hafgrímur, helped by Þrándur, killing the brothers. Brestir's son Sigmundur later avenges his father by killing Hafgrímur's son Össur, and Hákon jarl imposes a settlement.
Sigmundur defeats and kills the viking Vandill in a sea battle.

feud_name: Karl mærski and the king's tax
sides: ["Þrándur's kinsmen", "Leifur Össurarson and the king's men"]
summary: During the dispute over the king's tax, Þrándur's kinsmen Þórður lági and Gautur rauði kill the king's agent Karl mærski at the Faroese assembly; they are outlawed and banished.
Álfur afturkemba attacks Finnbogi in a cave and is killed by him.
A grazing dispute leads Uxi to attack Finnbogi, who kills him; the Brettingssons sue and ambush Finnbogi, and in the end a settlement bars Finnbogi from the Northern Quarter.
Þorgils kills vikings abroad in Þrándur's service.
Kolur kills Sörli, a thingman of Ásgrímur Elliðagrímsson, over his sister. Þorgils shelters Kolur, and Ásgrímur twice hires killers against Þorgils. Þorgils's lawsuit fails and kinsmen calm him down.
Þorgils kills the Norwegian Helgi, who mocked him; Helgi's brothers come for revenge but accept compensation.
Grímur hersir kills Öndóttur kráka while seizing property for the king; Öndóttur's sons and Önundur tréfótur burn Grímur in his house in revenge.
Grettir kills Þorkell krafla's servant Skeggi in a dispute over a food bag; Þorkell pays compensation and Grettir is exiled for three years.

feud_name: Grettir vs Björn and his brothers (Norway)
summary: Björn's provocations lead Grettir to kill him in Norway; Grettir also kills Björn's brothers, who seek revenge, and Earl Sveinn grudgingly accepts compensation.
Þorgeir kills Skúfur and Bjarni in Hundadalur; Þorgils Arason settles at once.

The Bjargsmenn quarrel with Þorbjörn öxnamegin and his kin: Grettir kills the kinsman Ferðalangur for insulting his dead father, Þorbjörn kills Grettir's brother Atli, and Grettir avenges Atli by killing Þorbjörn and his son. The case ends with compensation for Atli.
The outlaw Grímur tries to kill the sleeping Grettir and is killed by him.

feud_name: Killing of the outlaw Grettir at Drangey
summary: Þorbjörn öngull kills the outlaw Grettir on Drangey for the bounty; Öngull is outlawed and later killed in Constantinople by Grettir's brother Þorsteinn drómundur.
Gunnar settles old enmity with Örn of Vatnsendi, an ally of his enemies, by killing him in single combat; Örn's sister tries to avenge him by sorcery.
The robber Önundur kills Auðgísl abroad and is then killed by Hallfreður.

Hallfreður's affair with Kolfinna, Grís's wife, leads to fights: Hallfreður kills Grís's companion Einar, and Kolfinna's brother Brandur kills Hallfreður's brother Galti. Þorkell krafla's award offsets the killings.
Þorbjörn Þjóðreksson oppresses Hávarður and kills his son Ólafur; Hávarður and his allies take revenge, and Gestur Oddleifsson's settlement at the Althing awards triple wergild for Ólafur.

feud_name: Hrani vs Sigfús and his brother Hróaldur
summary: Sigfús kills Helgi krókur's shepherd Vakr over a sheep, and Hrani avenges Vakr. Sigfús's brother Hróaldur comes for revenge and kills Gauti, but is himself killed by Hrani.

feud_name: Kolfinnur and Búi, rivals for Ólöf
summary: Örn austmaður ambushes Kolfinnur, Búi's rival for Ólöf, and is killed; the rivalry continues until Kolfinnur's death.
Bersi and his foster-son Halldór kill Vali, his wife's brother, who was grazing Bersi's land.
Þorbjörn kills Barði, Þorgerður's shepherd, over grazing; Refur kills Þorbjörn after an insulting offer of compensation and is sent away.

feud_name: Refur vs Þorgils and his sons (Greenland)
summary: In Greenland Þorgils and his sons slander Refur as ragur, and Refur kills them all. Bárður and Gunnar besiege his fort; Refur escapes, killing Bárður during the chase.
In Niðarós the king's man Grani assaults Refur's wife, and Refur kills him.
Klaufi kills Hrani for grazing his kinsman's land; Grís pays compensation.
Klaufi kills Örn, who was riding Grís's horse; Grís pays compensation.

feud_name: Klaufi kills Björn and Sigurður (sheep round-up)
summary: Klaufi kills a father and son for driving his ewe astray at the sheep round-up.
Klyppur kills King Sigurður slefa for sleeping with his wife and is killed in the hall; the brothers are outlawed in Norway.
Jón and Auðólfur try to take Þórður's cloak by force and are killed; Skeggi arbitrates.
Þórður kills Ormur for pursuing his sister. Ormur's kinsmen Indriði, Össur and Sörli try to avenge him and are killed in turn, and Eiður's award and later agreements settle everything.

feud_name: Þorsteinn fagri vs Einar Þórisson and Hofsmenn
summary: Einar marries Þorsteinn fagri's betrothed and Þorsteinn kills him. Þorgils of Hof pursues Þorsteinn's brothers and dies with them, and Þorsteinn hvíti later reconciles with Þorsteinn fagri.

feud_name: Þorsteinn kills the forest robber Jökull
summary: Young Þorsteinn Ketilsson kills the forest robber Jökull to win fame.
Hrolleifur forces his attentions on Uni's daughter; Uni's son Oddur ambushes him, and Hrolleifur kills Oddur. Hrolleifur is later hunted down by the Ingimundarsons.
Már Jörundarson and Þorgrímur skinnhúfa claim land against the Ingimundarsons, and Högni falls in the fight; Þorsteinn's award settles the case.
Þorkell krafla kills Glæðir for taunting him; the case is settled with Guðmundur ríki at the assembly.
Hermundur kills Galti Óttarsson over Hallfreður's affair with Kolfinna; Þorkell krafla arranges a settlement.

A slander killing, lawsuits, an adultery killing and the killing of Hallsteinn set Helgi and Grímur Droplaugarson against Helgi Ásbjarnarson. Helgi Ásbjarnarson kills Helgi; Grímur avenges him and is outlawed.
After King Haraldur kills Þórólfur Kveldúlfsson, Kveldúlfur and Skalla-Grímur avenge him on the king's men and emigrate to Iceland.

Egill kills Bárður and Gunnhildur has a man of Þórólfur's killed. Later the inheritance dispute with Berg-Önundur leads to Egill's outlawry and his killing of Rögnvaldur Eiríksson. It continues until Egill buys his head at York.
A battle abroad in which Egill kills Aðils jarl right after Aðils's men kill Þórólfur.
Egill is ambushed on a tax-collecting mission and kills his attackers.

feud_name: Lambi vs Ketill gufa's runaway thralls
summary: Ketill gufa's runaway thralls burn Þórður Lambason inside his house. His son Lambi hunts them down and kills them.

feud_name: Þorsteinn Egilsson vs Steinar (grazing at Stakksmýri)
summary: Steinar's thralls graze cattle on Þorsteinn's land and Þorsteinn kills two of them. Egill arbitrates the lawsuit.

feud_name: Eiríkur rauði vs Eyjólfur saur's kin
summary: Eyjólfur saur kills Eiríkur's thralls and Eiríkur kills him and Hólmgöngu-Hrafn. Eiríkur is driven out of Haukadalur.
Jöður kills Hávar in a quarrel over a horse, and Hávar's 15-year-old son Þorgeir avenges him. A settlement follows.
Urged on by Sigurfljóð, the foster-brothers kill a robber father and son. Sigurfljóð buys them peace from Vermundur.
Þorgeir kills Þorgils Mársson over a whale and later his kinsman Gautur. Gautur's kinsman Þórarinn ofsi and Þorgrímur trölli kill Þorgeir, and Þormóður avenges his sworn brother in Greenland.
Þorgeir kills a man who did not answer him (Flateyjarbók text).
Þormóður kills the thrall Loðinn after being dragged across the floor. Skúfur settles it with sjálfdæmi.

feud_name: Björn the berserk vs Þorkell skerauki's sons
summary: Björn kills Ari in a holmgang for his wife and land, and Gísli the elder kills Björn.

feud_name: Gísli vs Þorgrímur & Börkur (killing of Vésteinn)
summary: Vésteinn's secret killing is avenged by Gísli on Þorgrímur, and later by Vésteinn's sons on Þorkell. Gísli is outlawed and finally killed.

feud_name: Þórir & Múli vs Helgi of Hjallar (grazing)
summary: A grazing dispute leads to Gunnar killing Þórarinn ákafi. Revenge ambushes by Helgi's sons and by Helgi end with their deaths, and the matter is settled.
Whale and land disputes lead to ambushes and a battle at Langeyri. Steinólfur and Hallur burn Ketilbjörn and Þórir takes revenge; Hallur dies and his son accepts a settlement.
Rivalry over Helga ends in a duel in Norway. Gunnlaugur kills Hrafn's kinsmen and both rivals die.

feud_name: Hörður & the Hólmverjar vs the district men
summary: The outlaw band on Geirshólmur is lured ashore and Hörður is killed by Þorsteinn gullknappur. Revenge is later sought on the slayers.
Styr kills Þórhalli over an unmarked sheep and mocks the son with a lamb as compensation. Gestur avenges his father and escapes abroad.
Barði's revenge for his brother Hallur ends in a battle on the heath, followed by a settlement.
Hrafnkell kills his shepherd Einar for riding Freyfaxi. Sámur wins the lawsuit and humiliates Hrafnkell, who later regains power.
Þórólfur kills Ingjaldur's brother Hallur over a catch of fish. Vigdís hides him and he escapes abroad.
Hrútur kills Eldgrímur, who was taking Þorleikur's horses by force.
Rivalry over Guðrún and a string of insults end with Bolli killing Kjartan. Revenge killings follow on both sides until a final settlement.
Auðgísl, backed by Snorri goði, kills Þorgils over a seized goðorð and is killed immediately.
A killing told in another saga and only mentioned here.

feud_name: Bolli Bollason vs Þórólfur stertimaður & the Hjaltasons
sides: ["Þórður of Marbæli & Bolli Bollason", "Þórólfur stertimaður & Hjaltasons"]
summary: Þórólfur kills a boy over a dead bull. Bolli has him outlawed and kills him, and a settlement follows (ch. 89).
Brandur kills Hárekur after being struck with a drinking horn. Compensation is paid.
A paternity case leads to a fight at Veisa where Ótryggur and Koðrán die. Eyjólfur breaks the settlement to avenge Koðrán, and compensation is then paid.
The Hánefur case and Vémundur's provocations lead to repeated killings. Steingrímur and Áskell die at the river ice and Skúta avenges Áskell. Þórir's sons finally kill Skúta and a settlement follows.
Hostility between Skúta and Glúmur; Glúmur's son Már kills Skúta's informer Hávarður.

feud_name: Valla-Ljótur & Svarfdælir vs Halli's kin & Guðmundur ríki
summary: Ljótur kills Halli after Halli extorts money from him, and Hrólfur gípa kills Þorvarður in breach of a truce. Björn avenges Þorvarður on Halli's kin, and Ljótur settles with Guðmundur.

It starts with Glúmur's killing of Sigmundur over Vitazgjafi. Arngrímur's killing of Steinólfur leads to the battle at Hrísateigur; Glúmur's false oath costs him Þverá and he is banished from the district.
Svartur kills Skíði over grazing and is outlawed. He then preys on Hof's sheep and the young Brodd-Helgi kills him.
Geitir kills Brodd-Helgi. Bjarni kills Tjörvi and, goaded by his stepmother, Geitir, then settles with Geitir's son Þorkell.
